why: The decisive event of the week is a negative, and it is the most useful fact in 22 readings: Google fetched the redesigned pillar and declined it. Request Indexing was submitted at 2026-11-13T04:06:28Z, the page was fetched 48 seconds later (lastCrawlTime 2026-11-13T04:07:16Z, pageFetchState SUCCESSFUL), and coverage is still 'Crawled - currently not indexed'. The caveat is real and stated: 48s may be the request's own priority fetch rather than an independent crawl. But the fetch read the 2026-11-11 redesign, which no crawler had read before, and the verdict did not change. Falsifiable test: if the pillar's coverage has not changed by 2026-11-19 — six days after a successful fetch of the final page — then no in-repo action (copy, title, sitemap, canonical, request) can index it, and every future cycle that offers one is lying to itself.

Indexation has no lever left inside this repository, and the evidence is now exhaustive rather than theoretical. The sitemap lastmod defect is fixed (`/` reads 2026-11-11 in production, was 2026-10-29). Request Indexing was refused once (quota) and accepted once (crawl, no index). The sitemap was contracted 25 → 22 → 21 URLs and the numerator fell 6 → 1 over the same period. All 21 URLs were submitted to Bing's URL Submission API and IndexNow on 2026-11-12, and Bing today is 0 indexed / 10 crawled / 11 unknown. Two independent engines have taken delivery of the inventory and kept one URL. What is left is site-level trust, which is bought by links from crawled publications and by time, not by a diff.

The only indexed URL is '/' and the only thing it can win is a brand click. It has 14 impressions and 2 clicks in 7d, both for 'btc500' @1.6; the single non-brand impression is at position 38. The five URLs that answer non-brand questions (pillar, /halving-dates, /simulator, /timeline, /when-to-sell-bitcoin-after-halving) have impressions but are not indexed, so there is no snippet to rewrite and no title to test. positions4to20 = 0. Test: if `/`'s 7d non-brand impressions are still ≤1 on 2026-11-27 while the pillar is declined, then search cannot produce a non-brand click before the 29 November buy date and the plan must say search is a 2027 channel.

Sessions are up 120% and that is not growth. 99 sessions / 31 users, but 70 sessions are Direct from 16 users (4.4 per user), engagement fell 31.3% from 57.8% and average duration 71.5s from 125.7s. 13 sessions out of 99 came from anywhere that is not us or google — facebook 6, t.co 3, chatgpt 2, x 1, bitcointalk 1 — and that 13 is the week's only positive movement (9 → 13). Test: while Direct stays above 60 sessions from under 20 users, no session total may be quoted without its named-source split, because the number is measuring the owner's dashboard.

Distribution has a measured ceiling of roughly thirteen sessions a week, and it is spread across five channels. facebook.com 6/6 from one unknown share of '/', t.co 3/3 from a 212-follower X account whose posts read 107 / 62 / 56 views, chatgpt.com 2/2 (10/10 in 28d), bitcointalk.org 1/1 from a rel="ugc" forum post by a zero-activity account, x 1/1. None of these produces a link. The one followed link (lopp.net, merged 2026-11-07T20:20:30Z, re-verified today: anchor present, 0 nofollow) has produced 0 sessions in 6 days and one crawl that ended in a decline. Test: 0 lopp.net sessions on 2026-11-21 closes the followed-link route as a strategy, and the remaining links must come from a publication that writes.

The ask ledger now has a working example and a dead one, and the contrast is mechanical. The BitcoinTalk post the owner actually sent on 2026-11-12 produced its first session within a day; the GitHub listing ask handed over three times produced nothing because it was never sent, and three handovers is the point at which §10(c) says the route is dead, not the owner. Meanwhile 4 of 5 cycle mandates executed and the site produced 1 session. The bottleneck is not the cycle's willingness; it is that everything the cycle can touch (sitemap, copy, crawl requests) has been proven not to move the number, and everything that could (a send, a link from a publication) sits with the owner.

The measurement instrument failed again, quietly, in a way the next cycle would have acted on. collect-results.mjs keeps one inspection file per date and takes whichever readdir returns first, so the 4-row file the cycle wrote at 04:09Z beat the 21-row file written at 07:32Z: review-input.json says `total: 4, indexed: 1` and the runner reported 'Indexed pages fell 3 -> 1' across two different populations. The count was right by luck (the 21-row read also says 1). A verdict that reads 1/4 and a target that reads 1/21 on the same day is how a series loses its meaning — and this is the same class of defect as the Referral-channel blindness fixed yesterday.

This is the twentieth consecutive non-improving review and the site is 16 days from the buy date it exists to serve ('16 days to buy' in the live countdown, 29 November 2026). The honest summary of 7 days: 8 runs, 4 of 5 mandates executed, 10 site commits, and the result is one forum session. Activity is not the constraint. The constraint is that a three-month-old domain with one followed link is not being served, and no cycle can change that by writing code.

A cycle may no longer offer sitemap, lastmod, Request Indexing, URL submission, merge, redirect, canonical or copy work as an indexation fix; its permitted output is one measurement plus one distribution action, and the PERFORMANCE block must print `indexation lever: none left (crawl 2026-11-13T04:07:16Z declined; Bing 0/21 after 21 submitted)`.

GROWTH_PROMPT.md — the `indexed` line in the mandatory PERFORMANCE block now requires the row count (`indexed X/21 (rows N of M)`), and a report with fewer rows than sitemap locs must be printed as `rows N of M — not a coverage reading` rather than as a fraction.
